Pisgah
PIZ-gah
proper noun
Hebrew Pisgah, “the cleft” or “the ridge,” the height of the mountain of Nebo from which Moses viewed the promised land.

📖 Biblical Definition

Pisgah was the height, or the ridge, of the mountain of Nebo in the land of Moab, over against Jericho. From its top the LORD shewed Moses all the land of promise, from Gilead unto Dan, and unto the utmost sea (Deu 34:1). It was a place of both vision and sorrow. Moses was bidden to get up into the top of Pisgah and lift up his eyes westward and northward and southward and eastward, and behold the land with his eyes, for he should not go over Jordan (Deu 3:27). And the LORD said, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob; I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither (Deu 34:4). The dictionary marks Pisgah as the mount of seeing but not entering. The law, in the person of its great minister, could bring Israel to the very border of the inheritance and show it from afar, but could not carry the people in; that was reserved for Joshua, whose name is the name of Jesus. So Pisgah teaches that the saints die in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and embraced them (Heb 11:13), assured that what the law shows from the height, Christ bestows in full.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The height of mount Nebo from which Moses viewed the promised land he might not enter.

expand to see more

PISGAH, the height or ridge of the mountain of Nebo in Moab.

From its top Moses beheld all the land of promise over against Jericho.

The LORD shewed him the land from Gilead unto Dan and the utmost sea.

Moses saw the inheritance with his eyes but might not go over Jordan.

It is the mount of seeing but not entering, a figure of the law.

📖 Key Scripture

Deu 34:1 — "And Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. And the LORD shewed him all the land of Gilead, unto Dan,"

Deu 3:27 — "Get thee up into the top of Pisgah, and lift up thine eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold it with thine eyes: for thou shalt not go over this Jordan."

Deu 34:4 — "And the LORD said unto him, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither."

Heb 11:13 — "These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it figures the law that shows the promise but cannot bring men in.

expand to see more

Pisgah has met no redefinition from the present age, being known to all who read of the death of Moses. The dictionary records the height that the reader may understand why Moses was permitted to see and not to enter, and what that withholding was made to teach.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the law brings men to the border of the inheritance and shows it from afar, but cannot carry them in. Moses, the great minister of the law, beheld the land from Pisgah yet died in Moab; it was Joshua, whose name is the name of Jesus, who led the people over Jordan. So the saints die in faith, seeing the promises afar off, assured that what the law displays from the height, Christ bestows in full.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “the cleft” or “ridge,” Pisgah names the height of Moses’ viewing.

expand to see more

Pisgah — Hebrew Pisgah, “the cleft” or “the ridge.”

It was the height of the mountain of Nebo in Moab.

It stood over against Jericho, across the Jordan from the land.

From its top Moses beheld all the land of promise.

He saw the inheritance with his eyes but might not enter it.

Usage

"Like Moses on Pisgah, the law brings men to the border and shows the promise from afar."

"The saints die in faith, having seen the promises afar off and embraced them."

"What the law displays from the height, Christ bestows in full to His people."
